note: This is a design artifact only. No Compose file was edited, no hostname was provisioned, no data was migrated, no runtime was promoted or deployed by this task. OSS-INFRA-PROFILES-001 is the sole later Compose writer that implements this contract; OSS-OBJECT-STORE-CUTOVER-001 consumes the storage disposition below.

cross_cutting_rules.health: Every profile-scoped service keeps its existing /readyz or /healthz HTTP probe or CMD-SHELL healthcheck unchanged; profile activation only changes which services start, never how an individual service reports health.
cross_cutting_rules.dependency: No profile's health or startup readiness may depend on MinIO/minio-init. Per storage-topology-decision.md, the accepted object-store backend is Google Cloud Storage. Inside a running service's startup/health path it is reached only by services/control-plane/bff/management_ai_store.py, and that dependency is env-gated/optional (falls back to local filesystem when PANTHEON_MGMT_AI_ATTACH_BUCKET is unset) rather than a startup precondition. `scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh` and `scripts/capture_canonical_telemetry_baseline.py` also read/write GCS objects, but as deploy-time/release-evidence tooling invoked outside any Compose service's own startup or healthcheck, so they do not become a new profile dependency edge. `depends_on: minio: condition: service_healthy` edges enumerated in storage-consumer-matrix.json are scheduled for removal by OSS-OBJECT-STORE-CUTOVER-001, not added to any new profile.
cross_cutting_rules.volume: A profile only mounts the durable volumes its own services already declare in docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.control.yml today (for example postgres-data, nats-data, *-data per service). No profile may share a volume across environments; this is already Architecture Invariant / Non-Goal #4 in SA.md ("No Cross-Environment Resource Sharing").
cross_cutting_rules.isolation: Profile activation must preserve SA.md's per-environment activation matrix (Dev/Ephemeral Staging/Prod Control/Prod Execution) and its Architecture Invariant #3 (Control and Execution Plane Segregation): the `execution` profile never runs on Prod Control, and no profile grants public ingress to anything other than the `core` profile's Caddy/Operator BFF edge.

core.sa_definition: Postgres, NATS, Caddy, Operator BFF, Projectors, Lifecycle

opt_in_never_default.reason: docker-compose.yml:1519-1528 declares `profiles: ["lifecycle-capacity-benchmark"]`; the file's own comment says it is a run-once harness "never started with the default stack". It is a distinct opt-in benchmark job, not part of core's default activation on any environment.

core.health_requirements: Postgres/NATS healthchecks gate every dependent service (existing service_healthy conditions retained). Operator BFF /readyz must stay green independent of GCS bucket configuration (attachment store degrades to local-filesystem, never blocks readiness).
core.dependency_requirements: postgres, nats only as hard startup dependencies. No minio dependency in this profile.
core.isolation_requirements: Only this profile's Caddy/Operator BFF edge may accept public ingress; core never carries live broker credentials.

research_owned_workers_conditional_on_re.reason: Each has a hard `depends_on: ... condition: service_healthy` on a `research`-profile service that is inactive in Prod Control: alpha-replication-worker -> research-orchestrator-svc (docker-compose.yml:381-385), training-session-preview-worker -> training-session-svc (docker-compose.yml:561-563), policy-learning-shadow-eval-scheduler -> policy-learning-svc (docker-compose.yml:666-670). Since `research` activation is `prod_control: NO`, these three workers cannot be started as prod_control singletons like the rest of the workers list; their effective activation follows `research`'s row (dev: YES, ephemeral_staging: NO, prod_control: NO, prod_execution: NO), not the workers-profile default.

workers.health_requirements: Each scheduler/consumer keeps its own liveness signal (health file or /readyz); prod_control runs each non-research-owned worker as a singleton (no horizontal replicas) per SA.md §5 footnote. The three research-owned workers above are simply not started in prod_control, so no singleton question arises there.
workers.dependency_requirements: postgres, nats, and the owning core-or-research service (e.g. reconciliation-drift-svc, evolution, source-ingest for the core-owned workers; research-orchestrator-svc, training-session-svc, policy-learning-svc for the research-owned workers) as declared today. No minio dependency.
workers.isolation_requirements: Workers never expose a public port; prod_control singleton constraint prevents duplicate outbox/reconciler consumption among the core-owned workers.

research.sa_definition: Model engines, MLflow, FinRL, Qlib, Data Scrapers
research.health_requirements: Dormant-smoke placeholders stay opt-in/inactive by default per OSS-INFRA-PROFILES-001's acceptance criterion to make unused research services opt-in; only research-orchestrator-svc/research-worker-gateway-svc/training-session-svc/policy-learning-svc are always-on in dev.
research.dependency_requirements: postgres required; nats optional per service. No minio dependency (research-orchestrator-svc currently declares PANTHEON_S3_* env only for posture, not I/O, per storage-consumer-matrix.json).
research.isolation_requirements: Never activated outside dev; heavy ML dependency images stay isolated from core/workers/management-ai/execution images (separate per-framework containers, no shared requirements file, per AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md OSS framework rule).

management-ai.health_requirements: Read-only diagnostic posture on prod_control: no durable-write command routes active; existing /readyz probes unchanged.
management-ai.dependency_requirements: operator-bff (core) must be healthy first; no minio dependency. The BFF's management_ai_store.py attachment path is the profile's only object-store touchpoint and stays env-gated to GCS/local-fallback per storage-topology-decision.md.
management-ai.isolation_requirements: Prod Control instance is read-only (no SOURCE_MANAGEMENT_COMMANDS_ENABLED / mutation routes armed); dev instance may enable durable-write local testing only.

execution.sa_definition: Runtime Manager, Broker Adapter, Exchange Adapter, Live LEAN
execution.note_two_distinct_compose_projects: This profile spans two separate Compose files with different service sets; they are not the same running stack and must not be merged into one flat service list.

prod_execution_opt_in.reason: docker-compose.exec.yml:195 declares `profiles: ["live"]`; not started by default even on Prod Execution.

execution.health_requirements: PANTHEON_LIVE_BROKER_ENABLED=false hardcoded outside the isolated Prod Execution VM (SA.md Architecture Invariant #5); readiness gates on paper/broker adapter health only.
execution.dependency_requirements: Dev/ephemeral-staging paper topology (docker-compose.yml) shares postgres/nats/signal-store with the `core` profile inside one compose project; signal-store (docker-compose.yml:89) is consumed only by this profile's paper-fleet-reconciler/paper-signal-producer/pantheon-paper-runtime, not by any core service, so it is scoped to `execution` rather than `core`. Prod Execution (docker-compose.exec.yml) is a wholly separate, isolated compose project that its own header comment says "intentionally excludes control-plane services such as operator-bff ... and telemetry" — it declares no postgres and no nats at all, so `core` supplies neither postgres nor nats to it. Instead docker-compose.exec.yml declares its own signal-store, and pantheon-paper-runtime has a hard `depends_on: signal-store, runtime-manager, broker-adapter, exchange-adapter (all condition: service_healthy)` (docker-compose.exec.yml:173-181); broker-adapter and exchange-adapter each in turn depend on runtime-manager being service_healthy. No minio dependency in either topology; execution never touches object storage in the current codebase (storage-consumer-matrix.json shows zero boto3/S3 usage repo-wide).
execution.isolation_requirements: Prod Execution VM has zero public IP / zero public ingress and accepts traffic only from Prod Control over private VPC peering, per SA.md Architecture Invariant #3; this profile must never be co-activated with prod_control.

unclassified_services_default_rule: Any docker-compose service not explicitly listed above and not carrying its own `profiles:` array (for example capital, registry, promotion, evaluation, persona, memory, consultation-svc, feedback, search-svc, source-ingest, evolution) remains scoped to `core` by default until OSS-INFRA-PROFILES-001 assigns it a profile during Compose convergence; this contract intentionally does not force every one of the ~80 declared services into a bucket, since that assignment is that task's implementation work, not this task's choice-and-design scope. Services that already declare their own Compose `profiles:` array (dormant-smoke placeholders at docker-compose.yml:2607,2639,2658,2679,2700,2713,2724; `openclaw-activation-ready-e2e` at :2544; `lifecycle-projector-capacity-benchmark` at :1519; `pantheon-lean-live` in docker-compose.exec.yml:195) are explicitly opt-in and are excluded from this default-to-core rule entirely — they are never started by any of the four environment activations above unless their named Compose profile is passed explicitly, so 'default' does not apply to them at all.
